ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher under NS-7; no account flag (no fake arrival confirmation).
ruling.reasoning:
Cancellation-fee branch: the driver cancelled the ride at 13:05:30 [F4], so the fee can only stand through NS-0's driver-cancels / rider-no-show branch into NS-1. NS-1 attaches the whole no-show test to the arrival confirmation: the driver must have confirmed arrival, been at the pickup at that moment, and then waited continuously at the pickup for more than three minutes until cancelling [NS-1].

Element (i) and (ii) pass: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 13:02:35 while 39 m from the pickup point, and his closest approach was 38 m at 13:05:30 [F6][F1], so the arrival confirmation was made inside the pickup zone [NS-1]. The trace settles both of these.

Element (iii) fails on the system records. The tap that constitutes the arrival confirmation was at 13:02:35 [F6], and the GPS record shows the driver within 200 m of the pickup for only 175 seconds (2 min 55 s) after that tap — below the NS-1 default of more than 3 minutes (180 s) [F6]. The 4 min 30 s the driver relies on runs from the platform's recorded arrival at 13:01:00 [F5], which is not the confirmation event he invokes; and the 3 min 15 s stationary window starts at 13:02:15, 20 seconds BEFORE his own tap [F3], so neither window is the post-tap wait NS-1 (iii) requires [NS-1]. The trace itself marks (iii) as failed [F6].

The driver's messages do not repair this. F10 ("More than 3 min already, I have to cancel") and F12 (his after-the-trip statement) are statements; where they conflict with the GPS/timeline record on the length of the post-tap wait they do not decide the point [F10][F12][F6], and F12 is a driver statement which, per G11, cannot establish the element either. The rider's "came out a minute after" account [F4] is likewise unsupported by any timestamped rider message [F11]; it plays no part in this ruling — the fee falls on the system records the driver himself cites.

Because an NS-1 element fails, the $6.61 charged [F7] is not chargeable and must be refunded in full under NS-2, irrespective of the fee equalling the published amount with no surge [F8][F4][F7]. Amount: the trace fixes it at the cancellation fee, $6.61 [F7][NS-2]. No flag_account: the trace's flag element is failed — the driver's tap was made while genuinely at the pickup (39 m), so there is no abuse of the arrival button [F6][F1][NS-2], and the profile fact that the driver has one prior upheld no-show dispute [F17] cannot by itself support an account action [RD-6].

Safety screen: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint — a pickup notice, a "more than 3 min already, I have to cancel" message, an after-the-fact wait statement, and a refund complaint, with no threats, insults, intimidation, sexual remarks or dangerous-driving allegation [F9][F10][F12][F4]; no traffic incident is recorded [F14]. safety_concern = none.

Evidence: the record settles every element needed — the cancellation event with its timestamp, the arrival confirmation, the GPS placement and the post-tap waiting interval are all present and hole-free [F4][F6][F2], so evidence_status = sufficient.

rejected_claims.reason: The 4 min 30 s inside 200 m runs from the platform's recorded arrival at 13:01:00 [F5], but the arrival confirmation the driver relies on is his 13:02:35 tap [F6]; NS-1 (iii) counts the wait from that confirmation, and the district records only 175 s inside the radius after the tap, so the (iii) element is not met [F6][NS-1].
Accepted, but it only satisfies NS-1 (ii) (tap at 39 m from pickup) [F6][F1][NS-1]; it does nothing for the separate waiting element (iii), which fails on the post-tap record [F6].

The 3 min 15 s stationary window starts at 13:02:15, 20 s before the driver's own 13:02:35 tap [F3][F6]; a wait that began before the arrival confirmation cannot satisfy NS-1 (iii), which runs from the confirmation until cancellation [NS-1].

F9 and F10 are driver chat messages, and F12 is an after-the-trip driver statement; on the length of the post-tap wait they yield to the GPS/timeline record showing 175 s inside the radius after the tap [F9][F10][F12][F6][NS-1].
Charging exactly the published $6.61 with no surge [F4][F7][F8] does not make the fee chargeable; NS-2 requires a full refund once any NS-1 element fails, and (iii) fails here [F6][NS-2].

The rider's uncorroborated timing account [F4][F11] is not what decides this case; the fee fails on the system records the driver himself cites — the failed (iii) element [F6][F5] — so the record-first rule operates in the rider's favour [NS-1][NS-2].

The driver's profile shows one prior upheld no-show dispute [F17], but RD-6 requires an established route-deviation case (RD-2 refund or a recorded RD-1 breach) before a flag; this is a fee-waiver case and the trace's flag element is failed, so no account action is warranted [F17][F6][RD-6].
The rider's clean profile [F16] is a background fact that cannot decide the case and was not used in the ruling; profile facts never decide a case alone [F16][NS-1].
